ShortDescription.Value: One bar showing the state of your city, where every reading opens what it is about.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Seety
Maybe the real city was the stats we saw along the way.
## Setup
1. Enable the mod. 2. Click the **gear** at the end of the bar. 3. Click the readings you want to keep, and drag the bar where you want it. 4. Click the gear again.
The bar is locked in place outside configuration mode.
## The bar
**Twenty-six readings**, each on or off as you like: happiness, health, unemployment, homelessness, workers, tourists, active problems, electricity, water, sewage, crematorium coverage, cemetery space, four school levels, parking, garbage, safety, fire safety, environment quality, post, traffic flow, land value, zone demand and public transport.
Three carry a second figure instead of a square of their own, because they are one question asked twice: health also holds hospital coverage, garbage also holds landfill space, and safety also holds free jail and prison cells. Open the reading and both are there, each still opening its own info view.
Nothing on the list is already on the vanilla HUD, and every figure mirrors the exact source the game uses for it - a number that disagrees with the game's own panels is worse than no number at all.
**More is always better.** The naturally negative figures - pollution, crime, cells occupied, schools filling up - are turned around and renamed, so a fuller, greener bar always means better, with no direction to remember per icon. Past a sensible limit a reading turns amber, then red; thresholds stay quiet in an empty city.
## Everything opens something
**Click a reading and it takes you to what it is about.** Most open the matching in-game info view. The rest open a window of their own - draggable, closeable:
> **Active problems** - every notification grouped by type and counted, worst first. Click a type and the camera goes to one of them, click again for the next, so you can work through them instead of hunting. A switch in the title bar hides the notification icons over the city.
> **Workers** - your workforce against the jobs that exist, on the same rows: people by education and age, who is employed, idle, working below their qualification, working outside the city or commuting in, and beside them the jobs at each level and how many nobody is doing. Every citizen counted one by one.
> **Happiness and demographics** - who actually lives here, age against education, with each band's share of the population drawn under it. A wide band of seniors is a wave of retirements coming; a wide band of teenagers is a school problem arriving in a few years.
> **Zone demand** - all six demands, and the five biggest reasons behind each. Commercial, industrial and office come apart per resource: what the city wants, how many businesses trade in it, how stocked their shelves are and how staffed they are. The game tracks all of it and never draws it, so a flat commercial bar stops being a mystery. Where a resource has a company behind it, the row flies you to the one losing most ground.
> **Selected journey** - a switch in the traffic window turns the jam list into the journey of whatever you have selected. Click a citizen or a vehicle and you get the street or transport line it is on now, every street and line still ahead of it with the distance along each, and where it all ends. It reads the route the game has already worked out, so nothing here is guessed. A step on public transport carries that line's own colour and number, and clicking it opens the line. Clicking the destination takes the camera there.
> **Schools**, **transport**, **traffic**, **parking** and **environment** - the fullest schools first, passengers and freight by mode, the worst jams by street - or, with a switch, the lines whose buses, trams, metros, trains or ferries are standing still - and the parts behind the combined readings. Where the game has its own panel for one of them, clicking goes there.
Some readings also carry a chart of how they got here.
## What it never does
Seety reads. It does not govern. Clicking a reading changes only which info view is showing and where the camera is pointing.
One option draws outside Seety's own bar: it can print the change beside the population and money figures on the game's bottom bar, which otherwise only shows it while you hover. The numbers are the game's own. It is off unless you turn it on.
Two other exceptions, both on the options page and nowhere near the bar. One is a field to add or remove money from your treasury, City Watchdog style - off to the side, typed in on purpose. The other fades the zoning cells drawn along your roads, for anyone who finds them loud: off unless you turn it on, it changes how those cells are drawn and nothing else, and switching it back off restores exactly the colours the game shipped.
## Before you install
Available in all twelve languages supported by the game. Free and open source under the MIT licence: [source on GitHub](https://github.com/merrinaf-tech/Seety).
If it saves you a few trips through the menus, you can [buy me a coffee](https://ko-fi.com/fabiozsche). Entirely optional - the mod is the same either way.
